headline: Cloudy with patchy fog Monday, then wetter, windier weather from Wednesday; next weekend could bring heavy rain but is uncertain.
summary: As of Sunday evening, high pressure overhead keeps western Washington dry but cloudy through Monday morning. Leftover moisture could produce patchy fog in fog-prone areas and limit visibility on the Monday morning commute, though forecasters call it a tough call between fog and a low cloud deck. Light easterly winds may cut down on fog in some places, and clearing probably won't come until the afternoon. Overnight lows were raised to above freezing because clouds are already filling in over the Southwest Interior. Light showers offshore should move inland Monday evening, with very light amounts. Tuesday afternoon turns drier and slightly warmer, though sunny breaks may be few, and temperatures stay near normal or a few degrees above. A series of stronger systems then arrives. Wednesday brings widespread rain and high-elevation snow, mostly over the Olympic Peninsula and North Cascades, with very little rain east of the Olympics. A stronger system follows into Friday morning, with about a half inch to an inch of water in the mountains, a tenth or two of an inch in the lowlands, and a few inches of new snow at higher elevations. Next weekend could bring the heaviest rain of the fall so far, but details are uncertain and depend on how far north a ridge of high pressure builds. Forecasters are fairly confident in the Wednesday-through-Friday systems because the model runs agree well, but the second week of November is highly uncertain. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect on land. A Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters and the west end of the Strait of Juan de Fuca runs from 1 AM Monday to 1 AM Tuesday because of building seas of 8 to 11 feet, and it may be extended for the outer coastal waters.
changes: Early-morning discussions focused on dense fog and a Friday system, with a possible Friday night break. By evening, the dense fog was over and only patchy Monday fog was expected, and the outlook gained a possible heavy-rain event next weekend. Lows were also raised to above freezing, replacing earlier talk of frost.
